To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new method for imitation learning from visual observations that outperforms prior methods on a set of continuous control tasks.

$i)$ imitation learning using visual observations is a viable approach to learning complex tasks in the Deep Mind control suite; $ii)$ the choice of the imitation loss function is critical to obtain good results, and

$i)$ imitation from pixel observations is possible, $ii)$ adversarial imitation learning is more sample efficient, but optimal transport is more robust to representation choice, and $iii)$ our implementation enables reproducible and easy-to-use benchmarking for imitation learning from pixel observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question. How can we leverage large amounts of visual data to learn control policies for dynamical systems with high-dimensional state and action spaces?
the following questions: $i)$ Can imitation learning from pixels achieve expert level performance in visual continuous control tasks?
the following questions: $i)$ How to learn representations that can be used to compute rewards for imitation learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for imitation learning from visual data in continuous control.
visual imitation learning from pixels is a challenging problem that is still in its infancy.
the best performing approach for visual imitation learning is the adversarial imitation learning method that we call VIME (Visual Imitation from Observation).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
imitation learning from pixels is feasible, but it is not as simple as it seems.
visual imitation is a challenging problem and we provide a set of recipes for solving it, with some caveats.
we show that imitation learning using only pixel observations is possible for continuous control tasks and that it is competitive to the state of the art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imitation learning from pixel observations for continuous control is a promising research direction, and we hope our work will inspire future research in this area.

visual imitation learning can be a powerful tool to learn complex behaviors in continuous control tasks from demonstrations, even when the demonstrations are not provided in the agent’s natural observation space.
